title: Align standard demo deck narrative with Redwood positioning (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + slide outline
creator: Talia Benson
project: Standard Sales Demo v1 (Demo Tenant + Talk Track + Deck)
description:
Problem
We need a single “Standard Demo Deck v1” narrative that (1) matches Redwood’s core positioning (production-grade inference: latency, cost, reliability, flexibility), (2) cleanly pivots between Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) without sounding like 3 separate products, and (3) supports persona-based branching (platform/ML/security) without re-authoring the deck per call.

Goals
- Define a slide outline that maps to the master talk track and the 4–6 known-good scenarios.
- Make the Hosted → Dedicated → Private story additive (same runtime + control plane + tools; increasing isolation/control).
- Keep claims “public-safe” for live demos (no hard pricing numbers, no brittle benchmark numbers; use ranges + show Console proof).
- Provide clear instructions for where screenshots come from (demo tenant) and what must be live vs screenshot.

Non-goals
- Vertical-specific decks (fintech/healthcare/telco) beyond small appendix callouts.
- Deep kernel/runtime architecture deck (we’ll link to optional 1-pager for technical deep dives).

Audience/personas to support
1) Platform Engineering / Infra: cares about reliability, fallbacks, isolation, ops, SLOs, ownership.
2) ML Engineering / Applied: cares about quality controls, evals, model choice, throughput/latency.
3) Security/Compliance: cares about deployment modes, retention, audit logs, RBAC/SSO, data residency.

Narrative principles (must hold on every run)
- Start with a concrete “production pain” (latency + cost + reliability + deployment constraints), not features.
- Prove with “show” > “tell”: route config, rollout/fallback, cost/latency dashboard, error analysis.
- Explain deployment modes as a spectrum:
  - Hosted API: fastest start; same API + Console; guardrails built-in.
  - Dedicated: predictable throughput + data isolation; SLA posture; enterprise controls.
  - Private: customer-managed networking/control plane options; VPC/on-prem; regulated workloads.
- Always include a Plan B if live behavior varies (screenshots + canned outputs + fallback route).

Proposed deck outline (v1)
0. Title slide (30s)
   - “Redwood Inference: production-grade LLM serving across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments”
   - Presenter names + agenda

1. The problem slide (60–90s)
   - “Inference is where apps fail: cost, latency, reliability, and deployment constraints.”
   - 3 bullets, no vendor bashing.

2. What Redwood is (60s)
   - One platform: API + runtime + Console
   - Differentiators: performance controls, reliability/fallback, unified deployment modes, observability

3. Demo flow / what we’ll show today (30s)
   - Scenario list with checkboxes (choose-your-own-adventure)
   - Expected timing: 12–15 min “standard”, 2–3 min “hosted mini”, 20+ min “deep dive”

4. Scenario A: Fast start on Hosted API (2–3 min)
   - Show: API call + streaming response
   - Proof: latency panel in Console, basic usage breakdown
   - Message: “No tradeoff between quickstart and production readiness; same controls later apply to Dedicated/Private.”

5. Scenario B: Cost & latency controls (3–4 min)
   - Show: token-level cost/latency breakdown, batching/caching toggle or profile comparison (where safe)
   - Guardrail: avoid exact $ claims; use relative statements + “your workload varies”

6. Scenario C: Reliability—routing + fallbacks + graceful degradation (3–4 min)
   - Show: route policy (primary model/version pinned) + fallback to compatible variant/region
   - Show: error analysis / incident-style panel (5xx, throttles) and how fallback prevents an outage

7. Deployment spectrum slide (Hosted → Dedicated → Private) (2 min)
   - Single visual: same API + Console; increasing isolation/control
   - Dedicated: reserved capacity + predictable throughput + SLA-backed posture
   - Private: VPC/on-prem options, customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations (high level)

8. Security & compliance posture (persona branch) (2–3 min)
   - Include only what we can confidently state and point to Security FAQ for details
   - Topics: retention defaults for demo tenant vs production, encryption in transit/at rest, RBAC/SSO/SAML posture (as applicable), audit logs (availability by deployment)

9. How teams adopt Redwood (Hosted → Dedicated → Private) (1 min)
   - Migration/upgrade story: keep endpoints stable; change deployment backing; keep routing/rollout policies
   - “Start in Hosted, graduate to Dedicated/Private when requirements demand.”

10. Next steps (30–60s)
   - “We can run your workload”: eval harness, prompt set, quality regression checks
   - Trial / Dedicated sizing / Private architecture review

Appendix (optional)
A1. Competitive framing (only if asked): where we win (production economics, flexibility, reliability)
A2. Architecture overview (runtime + control plane) for technical deep dive
A3. Data residency / regions slide variant for EMEA

Slide guidance: what must be live vs screenshot
- Must be live: 1 streaming response, 1 route config view, 1 dashboard view (latency/cost), 1 fallback demonstration (can be simulated via throttling toggle if safe)
- Can be screenshot: before/after comparisons, historical trends, long dashboards, any brittle benchmark visual

Claims policy (important)
- No hard pricing numbers. Acceptable: “usage-based”, “reserved capacity contracts”, “contact us for pricing.”
- No absolute benchmark numbers unless approved in “Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs”. Prefer: “typical range” + “we’ll validate on your workload.”
- Avoid implying data retention/audit logging features in Hosted if not available; use deployment-qualified statements.

Deliverables
- A finalized slide outline with speaker intent per slide (1–2 sentences) and “what to click/show” notes.
- A “Persona branch” tag per slide: Platform / ML / Security (primary + secondary).
- A checklist for screenshots required (and owners) aligned to Demo Tenant dashboards.

- Confluence: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/demo-tenant-security-faq.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/competitive/demo-objection-handling-competitive-notes.json

Acceptance criteria
- Outline approved by PMM (Soojin) + SE owner (Markus) + Product (Nikhil/Marissa) with no “untrue in product” steps.
- Each slide has: objective, persona tag, live vs screenshot tag, and source of truth (tenant view / screenshot link / doc).
- Deck supports a 2-minute hosted mini-demo variant by hiding optional sections (no re-authoring).
- Dedicated/Private claims reviewed against Security FAQ and product reality; no ambiguous language.

Open questions
- Do we want a single deck with “mode” callouts, or 1 base deck + 2 thin variants (Dedicated/Private appendix)? Current recommendation: single base deck + appendix variants.
- What is the minimum set of Console screenshots we must keep updated each release? Propose: route policy, cost dashboard, error analysis panel, rollout view.

Risks
- Drift between deck steps and Console UI changes; needs a lightweight change governance process (see PM-1843).
- Over-claiming security/compliance for Hosted; ensure we qualify by deployment mode.
- Live demo flakiness; outline must include Plan B paths per scenario.
